extracted.intended_audience: Owners, operators, and manufacturers of stationary sources (incinerators, municipal waste combustion units, CI/SI internal combustion engines), state/tribal air agencies, and facility compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of the New Source Performance Standards (Part 60) headings covering applicability, emission and operating limits, monitoring, testing, recordkeeping, reporting, operator training/certification, state plan/model rule requirements, and related tables/equations for a variety of source categories (incinerators, CISWI, OSWI, CI/SI engines, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this subpart apply to my [unit]? / Am I subject to this subpart?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears across many subparts (e.g., Subparts BBBB, CCCC, DDDD, EEEE, FFFF, IIII, JJJJ) and is the first step to determine regulatory coverage for a given unit or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: What definitions must I know?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each subpart includes specific definitions that determine applicability, standards, and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limits / Emission limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: What emission limits must I meet? By when?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both numeric emission limitations and effective dates; appears for incinerators, municipal waste combustion units, engines, and model rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating limits
rubrics_metrics.description: What operating limits must I meet and by when?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating parameters that must be established and maintained to demonstrate compliance (e.g., wet scrubber operating limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance testing / stack tests
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I conduct the initial and annual performance test? What types of stack tests must I conduct? What test methods must I use to stack test?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes initial, annual, and repeat testing, applicable test methods, schedules, and possible exceptions to testing frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I demonstrate initial compliance with the emission limitations and establish the operating limits? By what date must I conduct the initial performance test? By what date must I conduct the initial air pollution control device inspection?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and deadlines for demonstrating compliance when a unit first becomes subject to the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I demonstrate continuous compliance with the emission limitations and the operating limits? By what date must I conduct the annual performance test? May I conduct performance testing less often? May I conduct a repeat performance test to establish new operating limits?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing demonstration methods, frequency, and options for repeat tests to reset operating limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring equipment and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: What monitoring equipment must I install and what parameters must I monitor? What continuous emission monitoring systems must I install?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies required CEMS, opacity monitors, or other parameter monitors and the process units/parameters subject to monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS data use and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: How are the data from the continuous emission monitoring systems used? How do I make sure my continuous emission monitoring systems are operating correctly? What is my schedule for evaluating continuous emission monitoring systems?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses data application (compliance demonstration, averaging), performance checks, and evaluation schedules (including Appendix B/F references).

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS validation, exemptions, and schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Am I exempt from any appendix B or appendix F requirements to evaluate continuous emission monitoring systems? What is my schedule for evaluating continuous emission monitoring systems?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers circumstances for exemptions from validation/test requirements and timing for evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum monitoring data and enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the minimum amount of monitoring data I must collect with my continuous emission monitoring systems and is the data collection requirement enforceable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum data completeness requirements and whether failure to collect data is an enforceable violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting 1-hour arithmetic averages
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I convert my 1-hour arithmetic averages into appropriate averaging times and units?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures/formulae for converting monitoring averages to the regulatory averaging times/units (often referenced across subparts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is required for my continuous opacity monitoring system and how are the data used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for COMS installation, operation, data recording, and how opacity data are applied for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other monitoring requirements / continuous parameter monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Must I meet other requirements for continuous monitoring? How do I monitor the load of my unit? How do I monitor the temperature of flue gases at the inlet of my particulate matter control device? How do I monitor the injection rate of activated carbon?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers non-CEMS parameters (load, temperature, injection rate) and required monitoring approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring when systems unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: What must I do if any of my continuous emission monitoring systems are temporarily unavailable to meet the data collection requirements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for handling monitoring downtime and requirements for alternative monitoring or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stack test scheduling and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: What schedule must I follow for the stack testing? May I conduct stack testing less often? May I deviate from the 13-month testing schedule if unforeseen circumstances arise?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular testing intervals, possibilities for reduced frequency, and provisions for unforeseeable delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other monitoring validation requirements (tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for validating continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) and requirements for continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) (see tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to tables (e.g., Table 6, Table 7) for validation and CEMS-specific numeric/technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: What records must I keep? Where must I keep my records and for how long? What records must I keep for operator training and certification? What records must I keep for stack tests? What records must I keep for continuously monitored pollutants or parameters?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies record types, retention periods, formats, and location requirements; different record types for training, testing, CEMS, and special controls (e.g., activated carbon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: What reports must I submit and in what form? What are the appropriate units of measurement for reporting my data? When must I submit the initial report? What must I include in my initial report? When must I submit the annual report? What must I include in my annual report? What must I do if I am out of compliance with the requirements of this subpart? If a semiannual report is required, when must I submit it? What must I include in the semiannual out-of-compliance reports? Can reporting dates be changed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers reporting schedule, content, units, out-of-compliance reporting, semiannual/annual/initial reports, and requests to change reporting dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation and out-of-compliance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: What else must I report if I have a deviation from the operating limits or the emission limitations? What must I include in the deviation report?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required contents of deviation reports and additional notifications (e.g., for qualified operator accessibility deviations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress and compliance schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: What are my requirements for meeting increments of progress and achieving final compliance? When must I complete each increment of progress? What must I include in the notifications of achievement of increments of progress? When must I submit the notifications of achievement of increments of progress? What if I do not meet an increment of progress?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milestones, notification requirements, timing, and remedies/notifications for missed increments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste management plan
rubrics_metrics.description: What is a waste management plan? When must I submit my waste management plan? What should I include in my waste management plan?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and timing requirements for waste handling plans required for incinerators and related units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preconstruction siting analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Who must prepare a siting analysis? What is a siting analysis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for preconstruction siting analyses including responsible parties and necessary content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator training and qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the operator training and qualification requirements? When must the operator training course be completed? How do I obtain my operator qualification? How do I maintain my operator qualification? How do I renew my lapsed operator qualification? What site-specific documentation is required? What if all the qualified operators are temporarily not accessible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both general and plant-specific training, qualification timelines, documentation, and contingency procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator certification (municipal waste combustion units)
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of operator certification must the chief facility operator and shift supervisor obtain and by when must they obtain it? After the required date for operator certification, who may operate the municipal waste combustion unit? What if all the certified operators must be temporarily offsite?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific certification requirements and operational restrictions tied to municipal waste combustion units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good combustion practices and operating requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the operating practice requirements for my municipal waste combustion unit? What happens to the operating requirements during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good combustion practice obligations and exceptions or different handling during SSM (startup/shutdown/malfunction) periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model rule / State plan requirements and use of model rule
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the 'model rule' in this subpart? How does the model rule relate to the required elements of my state plan? What are the principal components of the model rule? Is a state plan required for all states? What must I include in my state plan? Is there an approval process for my state plan? What if my state plan is not approvable? Is there an approval process for a negative declaration letter? What compliance schedule must I include in my state plan? What authorities will not be delegated to state, local, or tribal agencies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for state agencies on preparing and submitting required State plans under CAA sections 111(d)/129(b)(2), including model rule use and approval/negotiation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title V Operating Permits
rubrics_metrics.description: Am I required to apply for and obtain a Title V operating permit for my unit? When must I submit a Title V permit application for my new/existing unit?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines when Title V permitting is required and applicable timing for application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air Curtain Incinerators (ACIs) specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: What is an air curtain incinerator? What is yard waste? What are the emission limits for air curtain incinerators that burn 100 percent yard waste? How must I monitor opacity for air curtain incinerators that burn 100 percent yard waste? What are the recordkeeping and reporting requirements for air curtain incinerators?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized definitions, emission limits, monitoring (opacity), and recordkeeping/reporting tailored to ACIs and to specific fuel/feedstock cases (yard waste, wood waste, clean lumber).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary-use incinerators and disaster recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the requirements for temporary-use incinerators and air curtain incinerators used in disaster recovery?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary or emergency-use provisions affecting monitoring, reporting, and compliance timetables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations
rubrics_metrics.description: What equations must I use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed calculation methods for converting monitoring data and demonstrating compliance; sections reference specific equation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables providing Model Rule—Compliance Schedules and Increments of Progress; Emission Limitations (various tables for different unit types/dates); Operating Limits for Wet Scrubbers; Toxic Equivalency Factors; Summary of Reporting Requirements; Requirements for Validating Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS); Requirements for Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS); Requirements for Stack Tests; Requirements for Continuous Parameter Monitoring Systems (CEMS) etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical limits, operating parameter values, monitoring validation criteria, and reporting summaries are detailed in the referenced tables throughout the subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission standards for stationary compression ignition (CI) internal combustion engines
rubrics_metrics.description: What emission standards must I meet for non-emergency engines if I am a stationary CI internal combustion engine manufacturer? What emission standards must I meet for emergency engines if I am a stationary CI internal combustion engine manufacturer? How long must my engines meet the emission standards if I am a manufacturer of stationary CI internal combustion engines? What emission standards must I meet for non-emergency/emergency engines if I am an owner or operator of a stationary CI internal combustion engine? How long must I meet the emission standards if I am an owner or operator?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturer vs owner/operator obligations, distinctions for emergency vs non-emergency engines, and duration of applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fuel requirements for CI owners/operators
rubrics_metrics.description: What fuel requirements must I meet if I am an owner or operator of a stationary CI internal combustion engine subject to this subpart?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies fuel specifications, fuel-use restrictions, or labeling/installation deadlines where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and testing requirements for CI engines (by displacement)
rubrics_metrics.description: What are my compliance requirements if I am a stationary CI internal combustion engine manufacturer or owner/operator? What test methods and other procedures must I use if I am an owner or operator of a stationary CI internal combustion engine with a displacement of less than 30 liters per cylinder? ... with a displacement of greater than or equal to 30 liters per cylinder?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and test methods differ by engine size and application; tables and sections specify test cycles and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, reports, and records for CI owners/operators
rubrics_metrics.description: What are my notification, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements if I am an owner or operator of a stationary CI internal combustion engine?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers required notifications, labeling, recordkeeping, and report content/frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special requirements and general provisions for CI engines
rubrics_metrics.description: What requirements must I meet for engines used in Guam, American Samoa, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands? What requirements must I meet for engines used in Alaska? What emission standards must I meet if I am an owner or operator of a stationary internal combustion engine using special fuels? What General Provisions and confidential information provisions apply to me?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Region- or fuel-specific exceptions/requirements and applicability of General Provisions and confidentiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission standards and requirements for stationary spark ignition (SI) internal combustion engines
rubrics_metrics.description: What emission standards must I meet if I am a manufacturer of stationary SI internal combustion engines or equipment containing such engines? What emission standards and durations must I meet if I am an owner or operator of a stationary SI internal combustion engine? What fuel requirements and monitoring requirements apply to owners/operators? What are the compliance requirements for manufacturers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel structure to CI engine subpart with manufacturer vs owner/operator obligations, fuel and monitoring requirements, and compliance/testing provisions.
